detail.title: Compositional Heredity across Growth-Division Regimes
detail.summary: Multistable autocatalytic reaction networks exhibit compositional memory, allowing stable states to be maintained across growth-division cycles. This memory is driven by the feedback between chemical kinetics and compartment growth, where stochastic transitions between states act as primitive mutations.
detail.reason: Notebook revision required by governance to integrate recent evidence regarding thermodynamic drivers of natural selection in prebiotic networks.

detail.title: Hysteresis vs. Memory in Autocatalytic Reaction Networks
detail.summary: Autocatalytic networks can store history-dependent states that influence future behavior. Distinguishing this memory from transient persistence requires identifying hysteresis loop closure and state-dependent reaction rates.
detail.reason: Synthesis-ready project requires a notebook to facilitate further focused research.
